messages:
sai: heads-up — ap-southeast1 nvme-hotwindow cohort is causing a provisioning stall, ~29 GPU attaches pending.
emma: seeing prolonged attach latencies and a tail of nvme read/write latencies. any kernel errors?
rafa: grabbed dmesg from gnode-apse-11:
```
[ 2100.123456] nvme0: I/O 0x1f4a2 timed out
[ 2100.123860] blk_update_request: I/O error, dev nvme0n1, sector 204800
[ 2101.500000] nvme_core: admin timeout
```
toni: this cohort got the new janitor overlay for ephemeral cleanup last deploy. janitor concurrent workers defaulted to 32 and kicked off at 00:05 local.
sai: timeline looks like janitor + scheduled scrub window + a big GPU batch at 00:08 = write-amplification + hotspot on a small set of lanes.
emma: iostat shows %util bouncing 95-100 on nvme0 but avgqu-sz small. suggests long per-request stalls rather than queue saturation.
ops-bot: ALERT: GPU_PROVISIONING_HOLD ap-southeast1: 29 pending at 3712345625
rafa: mitigation options: 1) throttle janitor/overlay cleanup (set concurrent_workers=2); 2) cordon noisy nodes and exclude pool from autoscaler; 3) run a soft-failover of pending attaches to healthy pools.
toni: applying hotpatch to maintenance: `janitor.concurrency=2` for label cohort=nvme-hotwindow. will taint the 9 most-affected nodes `nvme-hot:NoSchedule`.
sai: be mindful of spill costs — ops please confirm budget if we push >20% to us-west.
oncall: ops-bot created incident INC-2026-4521 and notified storage/hardware teams at 3712345650
emma: janitor throttle applied and cordons starting. moving only the pending attaches from tainted nodes to healthy pools.
rafa: attach success jumped from ~40% to ~86% after cordons & throttle. two nodes still show recurring admin timeouts; flagging for drive replacement.
toni: adding a temporary autoscaler rule: prefer pools with nvme.admin_timeouts==0 when scheduling attaches for 30m.
emma: follow-ups: 1) add a Grafana dashboard that correlates janitor concurrency, nvme %util, kernel I/O errs, and gpu-provisioner pending counts; 2) add alert for admin timeouts >2 in 5m; 3) change janitor default concurrency to 4 for fresh cohorts.
sai: also add a preflight check: if firmware rollout changes scrub/trim behavior, ensure janitor is disabled or concurrency low during the first 24h.
ops-bot: deploy started gpu-autoscaler-hotpatch with `--exclude-pool=apse1-nvme-hotwindow` at 3712345820
oncall: short-term plan: replace 2 drives, keep rest in monitored pool. re-enable janitor gradually in 2h with ramped concurrency.
rafa: logging note: surface nvme admin timeouts as a disk health SLI and add it to incident runbook.
emma: I'll file a brief postmortem and update the runbook with the janitor/concurrency defaults and rollout checklist. :thumbsup:
sai: cost tradeoff accepted for SLA. schedule sync tomorrow to lock in firmware+janitor coordination. :coffee:
